1.w: (40:25) “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook and tie down its tongue with a rope?

2.w: Can you put a cord through its nose or pierce its jaw with a hook?

3.w: Will it make numerous supplications to you; will it speak to you with tender words?

4.w: Will it make a pact with you, so you could take it as your slave for life?

5.w: Can you play with it, like a bird, or tie it on a leash for your girls?

6.w: Will partners bargain for it? Will they divide it up among the merchants?

7.w: Can you fill its hide with harpoons or its head with fishing spears?

8.w: If you lay your hand on it, you will remember the fight. Do not do it again!

9.w: (41:1) See, his expectation is wrong; he is laid low even at the sight of it.

10.w: Is it not fierce when it is awakened? Who is he, then, who can stand before it?

11.w: Who has confronted me that I should repay? Everything under heaven belongs to me!

12.w: I will not keep silent about its limbs, and the extent of its might, and the grace of its arrangement.

13.w: Who can uncover its outer covering? Who can penetrate to the inside of its armor?

14.w: Who can open the doors of its mouth? Its teeth all around are fearsome.

15.w: Its back has rows of shields, shut up closely together as with a seal;

16.w: each one is so close to the next that no air can come between them.

17.w: They lock tightly together, one to the next; they cling together and cannot be separated.

18.w: Its snorting throws out flashes of light; its eyes are like the red glow of dawn.

19.w: Out of its mouth go flames; sparks of fire shoot forth!

20.w: Smoke streams from its nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning rushes.

21.w: Its breath sets coals ablaze, and a flame shoots from its mouth.

22.w: Strength lodges in its neck, and despair runs before it.

23.w: The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm on it, immovable.

24.w: Its heart is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone.

25.w: When it rises up, the mighty are terrified; at its thrashing about they withdraw.

26.w: Whoever strikes it with a sword will have no effect, nor with the spear, arrow, or dart.

27.w: It regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.

28.w: Arrows do not make it flee; slingstones become like chaff to it.

29.w: A club is counted as a piece of straw; it laughs at the rattling of the lance.

30.w: Its underparts are the sharp points of potsherds; it leaves its mark in the mud like a threshing sledge.

31.w: It makes the deep boil like a cauldron and stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment,

32.w: It leaves a glistening wake behind it; one would think the deep had a head of white hair.

33.w: The likes of it is not on earth, a creature without fear.

34.w: It looks on every haughty being; it is king over all that are proud.”
